claude_take: This week's AI news splits into two very different bets: Anthropic pricing a roughly trillion-dollar IPO and Alibaba rushing out a bare-bones Qwen4-Max preview are both betting that speed and scale win, while DeepMind's quieter work getting AI agents to formally verify Signal's encryption is betting that AI's real value is making things provably trustworthy. That split lands awkwardly next to COP31's pleas for climate urgency and windfall taxes, since the compute build-out funding both AI bets is itself an energy problem nobody in Antalya can ignore. And Burberry's unglamorous return to profit, alongside a poll showing most Americans still feel squeezed by the cost of living, is a reminder that the real economy doesn't care how a model benchmarks.
claude_take_title: The Real Economy Doesn't Care About Benchmarks

items.headline: Anthropic Sets IPO Price Range, Targets Nasdaq Debut This Week
items.summary: Updating earlier coverage of its roadshow, Anthropic has set terms for its IPO, pricing shares at $70 to $78 and targeting a valuation near $1 trillion (about $1.4 trillion fully diluted), with trading set to begin on Nasdaq under the ticker ANT on November 19. It would rank among the largest tech listings ever, testing investor appetite for AI companies after a volatile stretch for tech stocks.

items.headline: Alibaba Opens Early Preview of Its Qwen4-Max Flagship Model
items.summary: Alibaba's Qwen team opened a public preview of Qwen4-Max, the first release from its next-generation flagship family, adding agent-first coding support and a 1-million-token context window. The preview is available through Alibaba's Token Plan, Qwen App and coding tools, though the company has not yet disclosed parameter counts or benchmark scores, and the preview endpoint is due to retire on November 25.

items.headline: Google DeepMind Uses AI Agents to Formally Verify Signal's Encryption
items.summary: Google DeepMind's AlphaProof Code project had AI agents write more than six million lines of machine-checked proof verifying key security properties of the real code behind Signal's encrypted messaging protocol, with every proof validated by the Lean theorem prover rather than trusted outright. Researchers tested the method by reintroducing two previously fixed bugs, and the system caught both. Signal's chief technology officer called the result a major breakthrough, though DeepMind frames it as a research project rather than a deployable product.

items.headline: Foundry Updates Nuke Stage Virtual Production Platform, Teases macOS Edition
items.summary: Foundry released version 1.2 of Nuke Stage, its in-camera VFX and virtual production platform, marking the tool's second major update since launch. The company also previewed an upcoming macOS edition aimed at independent artists and smaller studios, extending real-time, on-set visual effects workflows beyond the large facilities that have driven virtual production adoption so far.

items.headline: COP31 Leaders' Summit Draws Record Crowd as Guterres Urges Windfall Taxes
items.summary: The UN's COP31 climate summit in Antalya, Turkey drew roughly 92,000 attendees to its Leaders' Summit, making it the largest COP in history. UN Secretary-General Antonio Guterres urged faster emissions cuts, more adaptation finance and windfall taxes on oil and gas companies, while leaders and philanthropic partners announced more than $480 million in new funding to cut methane and other short-lived pollutants. Negotiators are still working toward a final cover decision as the conference, which runs through November 20, remains deadlocked over money and a fossil-fuel phase-out.

items.headline: Reuters/Ipsos Poll Finds Americans Still Squeezed by the Cost of Living
items.summary: A Reuters/Ipsos poll conducted November 6-9 found President Trump's approval rating holding at 32%, near the lowest of his career, with just 21% of US adults approving of his handling of the cost of living. Sixty-five percent of adults disapproved of his overall performance, including 50% who disapproved strongly, in a survey of 1,705 adults with a margin of error of about 2 points. The result points to persistent economic strain shaping household behavior heading into the holiday season, regardless of broader market optimism.

items.headline: Burberry Returns to Profit as New Chair Takes Over Mid-Turnaround
items.summary: Burberry's interim results showed revenue up 6% to £1.10 billion and adjusted operating profit more than tripling to £62 million, with net profit of £6 million reversing a £26 million loss a year earlier; shares rose roughly 7-8% on the news. The results also marked chair Gerry Murphy's planned departure, with William Jackson succeeding him, as CEO Joshua Schulman's 'Burberry Forward' turnaround strategy shows its clearest signs of traction yet.

items.headline: Martin Buber's I-Thou
items.summary: In 'I and Thou' (1923), Martin Buber distinguished two fundamental ways of relating to the world: 'I-It,' in which we treat other people, animals or even nature as objects to be used, known or managed, and 'I-Thou,' a direct, mutual encounter in which another being is met as a whole presence rather than a means to an end. Buber argued that a fully human life depends on cultivating I-Thou relations, even though I-It relations are unavoidable and necessary for ordinary functioning. The distinction still shapes how people think about intimacy, therapy and ethics, and offers a sharp lens on a moment when so much daily interaction, with algorithms, assistants and strangers alike, risks flattening into I-It.
items.summary_fr: Dans « Je et Tu » (1923), Martin Buber distingue deux manières fondamentales de se rapporter au monde : le « Je-Cela », où l'on traite autrui, les animaux ou même la nature comme des objets à utiliser, connaître ou gérer, et le « Je-Tu », une rencontre directe et réciproque où l'autre est accueilli comme une présence entière plutôt que comme un moyen. Buber soutenait qu'une vie pleinement humaine exige de cultiver des relations Je-Tu, même si les relations Je-Cela restent inévitables et nécessaires au fonctionnement quotidien. Cette distinction continue d'éclairer la façon dont on pense l'intimité, la thérapie et l'éthique, et offre un angle incisif à une époque où tant d'interactions quotidiennes, avec des algorithmes, des assistants ou de parfaits inconnus, risquent de se réduire au Je-Cela.
